docs.title: When to Use Templates
docs.text:
Use templates when:

  • Configuration follows a predictable pattern
  • Multiple tables share similar validation structure
  • Logic is parameterizable
  • You want centralized pattern updates

Avoid templates when:

  • Each table requires unique logic
  • Configuration is simpler without abstraction
  • Parameterization obscures intent
  • Modular config directories are sufficient

docs.title: Templates vs Modular Config
docs.text:
Template System Modular Config Single Jinja2 file Directory structure Loop-based generation Explicit file per table Centralized pattern Distributed configuration Tag invocation Path invocation

Preference: Use modular config for explicit control. Use templates for standardized patterns across many similar tables.

docs.title: Config Resolver Logic
docs.text:
# neco_dq/config/config_resolver.py:159-180

def resolve_config(config_ref: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Supported inputs:
    - path to YAML file (single-file config)
    - path to modular config directory
    - template registry tag
    """
    path = Path(config_ref).expanduser()

    if path.exists():
        path = path.resolve()

        if path.is_file():
            return _resolve_single_file_yaml(path)

        if path.is_dir():
            return _resolve_modular_config(path)

    if isinstance(config_ref, str):
        return _resolve_template_tag(config_ref)

    raise ValueError(f"Unable to resolve config reference: {config_ref}")

docs.title: Template Tag Resolution
docs.text:
# neco_dq/config/config_resolver.py:32-42

def _resolve_template_tag(tag: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_REGISTRY.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Template registry not found at {DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_REGISTRY}")

    registry = _load_yaml(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_REGISTRY)

    if tag not in registry:
        raise KeyError(f"Template '{tag}' not found. Available: {list(registry.keys())}")

    resolved_path = Path(registry[tag]).expanduser().resolve()
    return _resolve_single_file_yaml(resolved_path)

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create Jinja2 YAML template file
  2. Add entry to template_registry.yaml
  3. Document expected context structure
  4. Test with representative data

docs.title: Example: Custom Bronze Template
docs.text:
1. Create template

# neco_dq/config/bronze/bronze_minimal_template.yaml

bronze:
  tables:
{% for t in tables %}
    - catalog: "{{ t.catalog }}"
      schema: "{{ t.schema }}"
      table: "{{ t.table }}"
      checks:
        row_count:
          min_rows: {{ t.min_rows | default(1) }}
          severity: critical
{% endfor %}

2. Register

# neco_dq/config/template_registry.yaml

silver_standard: config/silver/silver_standard_template.yaml
ge_standard: config/ge/ge_standard_template.yaml
bronze_minimal: config/bronze/bronze_minimal_template.yaml  # NEW

3. Invoke

config = resolve_config("bronze_minimal")

docs.title: Determinism Requirement
docs.text:
Templates must produce deterministic output.

Forbidden:

  • Randomness
  • Time-dependent behavior (unless explicit in context)
  • External API calls during rendering
  • Filesystem reads beyond template file

Allowed:

  • Pure Jinja2 logic
  • Context variable access
  • Type checking and conditionals
  • Filters and loops

docs.title: 1. Generic Structure
docs.text:
Templates define structure, not business logic.

# GOOD: Generic
{% for t in tables %}
  - table: "{{ t.name }}"
    check: row_count
    min: {{ t.threshold }}
{% endfor %}

# BAD: Hardcoded business logic
{% for t in tables %}
  - table: "{{ t.name }}"
    check: value_range_validation  # Too specific
{% endfor %}

docs.title: 2. Explicit Context
docs.text:
Document expected context variables.

# Required context:
# - tables: list[dict]
#     - catalog: str
#     - schema: str
#     - table: str
#     - pk_id: str | list[str]
#     - status_column: str (optional)

docs.title: 3. Fail-Safe Defaults
docs.text:
Provide sensible defaults where possible.

severity: {{ severity | default("error") }}
blocking: {{ blocking | default(true) }}

docs.title: 4. Readable Output
docs.text:
Generated YAML should be human-readable.

Use proper indentation and structure.

docs.title: Template Not Found
docs.text:
KeyError: Template 'unknown' not found. Available: ['silver_standard', 'ge_standard']

Solution: Check template_registry.yaml for correct tag.

docs.title: Jinja2 Syntax Error
docs.text:
jinja2.exceptions.TemplateSyntaxError: unexpected '}'

Solution: Validate Jinja2 syntax. Common issues:

  • Missing {% endif %}
  • Unmatched braces {{ }}
  • Invalid variable names

docs.title: Undefined Variable
docs.text:
jinja2.exceptions.UndefinedError: 'pk_id' is undefined

Solution: Ensure context provides required variables.

Use {% if variable is defined %} for optional fields.

docs.title: Invalid YAML Output
docs.text:
yaml.scanner.ScannerError: mapping values are not allowed here

Solution: Template generated invalid YAML structure.

Validate Jinja2 indentation and syntax.

docs.title: Thresholds
docs.text: Many row-level checks support a threshold configuration that tolerates a certain number or percentage of failing rows before the check itself fails. Thresholds work the same way across the Bronze, Silver and Gold suites, so they're documented once here. Each suite page lists which of its checks honour a threshold.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
threshold:
  max_failure_percent: 5.0    # Allow up to 5% of rows to fail
  max_failure_count: 100      # Allow up to 100 rows to fail

Evaluation logic:

  • If both parameters are specified, both must be satisfied (AND logic).
  • If neither is specified, zero tolerance applies (the original strict behaviour).
  • A threshold can be defined at the check level or as a suite-level default.

docs.title: Where it applies
docs.text:
Not every check is threshold-based. Row-level checks that count failing rows support threshold; checks with their own tolerance semantics use a dedicated parameter instead (e.g. min_valid_percent, tolerance_abs, tolerance_percent, max_delay_hours) or are binary pass/fail. See the per-suite tables:

  • Bronze - supported checks
  • Silver - supported checks
  • Gold - supported checks

Threshold vs check-specific tolerance

If a check doesn't support threshold, it usually has a purpose-built tolerance knob documented in its Check Details entry. Look there before assuming a check is strict zero-tolerance.

The threshold keys themselves (max_failure_percent, max_failure_count) are unchanged. For how the check-specific tolerance and column keys are named, and the deprecated spellings they replace, see Parameter Naming Conventions.
Fixes from the review of the 1.4.0 check-parameter standardization.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• freshness works on DATE columns (all suites). Spark returns a DATE max as a Python date, which has no tzinfo, so the check failed with 'datetime.date' object has no attribute 'tzinfo' instead of measuring anything. A date is now read as midnight UTC of that day.
  • dq_policy.unknown_check_params is now honored in normal run_dq() runs: the orchestrator passes dq_policy to every suite, so error and ignore no longer behave as warn.
  • With unknown_check_params: error, invalid check parameters now fail the run (CheckConfigError) instead of being summarized as a suite crash that evaluated to a warning.
  • Resolving deprecated nested keys (history.tolerance_pct, lateness.column) no longer mutates shared default_checks, so every table using them is counted in the deprecation report.
  • Check IDs of multi-instance checks stay as in 1.3.0 for unchanged configs using deprecated keys (e.g. idempotency[key_column=id]); IDs are built from the config as written.
  • List-valued join columns now work as documented: gold_join_columns / silver_join_columns in reconciliation_expr (with a length check), and join_columns in cross_table_equality and temporal_consistency join on every listed column.
  • flow_completeness with list-valued join_columns no longer crashes when reporting missing records (failure stats listed the key list as a single nested item).
  • Gold coverage accepts a single join column given as a string (gold_join_columns: id); it was split into characters.
  • Investigation queries of the join-based silver checks (totals_consistency, cross_table_equality, temporal_consistency, flow_completeness) are now fully rendered, with one join condition per key column; previously they returned the raw template with unresolved placeholders.
  • Profiling suggestions are valid configs for the checks they target: _reason / _confidence / _comment annotations are no longer reported as unknown parameters (they failed the run under unknown_check_params: error); the trend suggestion now uses the name + history: {table, window, tolerance_percent} shape; bronze table_freshness and record_count_anomaly suggestions use max_staleness_days and max_deviation_percent.
  • trend, and volume with a name, now find their own history: the lookup uses the persisted check ID (trend, or trend[name=...] with several instances) instead of name, which never matched, so these checks always passed as "insufficient history".
  • volume history mode works on real history: the baseline is parsed from what volume itself writes (Volume OK: 123), not from a value= pattern it never emitted, so a history-only volume no longer passes regardless of the change. Failure messages now include the current value (Volume 4 deviation ...) so they also feed later baselines. History values are read back exactly, including scientific notation (1e+20, 1e-06), and trend / volume compare DECIMAL metrics without a type error.
  • cross_gold without left_table uses the table under validation as already filtered by row_filter / partition_filter, instead of reloading the whole table.
  • flow_completeness investigation queries apply source_filter inside a source-only subquery, so filters on join columns are no longer ambiguous.
  • reconciliation_expr rejects gold_join_columns without silver_join_columns (or vice versa) instead of silently comparing against all Silver rows.
  • Great Expectations converts to pandas only the columns its expectations read (column keys, column_list, names used in row_condition, and the columns of integrity, no_duplicate and multicolumn_sum). Before, the whole table was converted, so a timestamp past 2262-04-11 (the pandas datetime64[ns] limit, e.g. a 2999-12-31 "no end date" sentinel) in any column crashed the table as engine_crash and none of its expectations ran. A far-future timestamp in a column that is checked still crashes the table.
  • Great Expectations engine_crash rows are written with their run_timestamp and a run_id instead of NULL and "None", so dashboards that pick the latest run by run_timestamp show the crash. Their details is a plain message (Check error: ...) like other rows. data_filter rows now carry the same run_id as the expectation rows of their table.
  • record_count_anomaly reports Count went from 0 to N (no previous rows to compare against) when the previous count was 0, instead of Count deviation 0.0% exceeds ...% limit. The check still fails.
  • Lakeview dashboard: the regression datasets (regression_summary, regression_detail) keep checks of the same schema.table in different catalogs (and suites) apart; the detail table shows catalog.schema.table. Regenerate dashboards to pick this up.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: • All configuration examples use canonical check parameters (no deprecated keys, no parameters a check does not accept); the deprecated-keys tables in Naming conventions are complete, and the incorrect note saying trend keeps tolerance_pct was removed. cross_table_equality / temporal_consistency docs no longer advertise unsupported left_catalog / right_catalog keys.
Check-parameter standardization: a single naming convention across every check, with a non-breaking deprecation path for the old keys.

docs.title: Declarative check-parameter schema (neco_dq/core/registry/check_param_schema.py)
docs.text: A single source of truth for every check's configuration surface: required keys, optional keys, deprecated-key aliases, and forbidden keys. It drives three things that used to drift independently: alias resolution, unknown-key validation, and the machine-readable inventory cross-checked against the suites' _require_cfg calls (new consistency test).

docs.title: Config-parameter validation (dq_policy.unknown_check_params)
docs.text:
Unknown top-level check parameters (typically typos) are now surfaced, with a suggested correction via edit-distance (e.g. kye_columns → "did you mean 'key_columns'?"). Strictness is configurable:

Setting Behavior warn (default) Logs a warning and continues (honors the non-breaking policy) error Fails the run with a clear message naming the check and key ignore Restores the pre-validation behavior

Forbidden keys (parameters that no longer apply because the current table is implicit, e.g. target_* on flow_completeness) are surfaced the same way.

docs.title: Deprecation reporting
docs.text: Deprecated-key usage is collected during a run (deduplicated per (check, old_key), with the count of distinct tables that used it) and is available programmatically in the run summary under deprecations. A dedicated summary section renders it in verbose runs only (run_dq(verbose=True)), so normal runs stay clean. Nothing is printed mid-execution.

docs.title: json_schema supports BINARY columns
docs.text: json_schema now accepts BINARY columns (raw UTF-8 JSON bytes, as stored for raw Kafka payloads in Bronze): the column is decoded to STRING before from_json, so field/type/allowed-value validation works without a separate decode step. STRING and STRUCT / ARRAY<STRUCT> columns are unchanged. Investigation-query templates decode the column too, so they remain runnable against the physical table.

docs.title: Parameter renames (old keys still accepted, now deprecated)
docs.text:
All renames below are non-breaking: the old key keeps working via an alias and is flagged as deprecated. Templates, docs, and generated configs now emit the new names. The old keys are scheduled for removal in the next major release, at which point they become validation errors.

Bronze

Check Old key New key record_count_anomaly allowed_deviation_percent max_deviation_percent table_freshness max_days_stale max_staleness_days

Silver

Check Old key New key idempotency, status_transition key_column key_columns cardinality min min_count totals_consistency join_key, catalog, tolerance join_columns, detail_catalog, tolerance_abs cross_table_equality join_key, tolerance join_columns, tolerance_abs temporal_consistency join_key, left_timestamp, right_timestamp join_columns, left_timestamp_column, right_timestamp_column row_temporal_consistency left_timestamp, right_timestamp left_timestamp_column, right_timestamp_column flow_completeness join_key, tolerance_pct join_columns, tolerance_percent lateness lateness.column lateness.timestamp_column

Gold

Check Old key New key reconciliation_expr gold, silver (expr), tolerance gold_expr, silver_expr, tolerance_percent coverage tolerance_pct, join_keys, gold_join_keys, silver_join_keys tolerance_percent, join_columns, gold_join_columns, silver_join_columns volume min, max, history.tolerance_pct min_value, max_value, history.tolerance_percent cross_gold tolerance tolerance_abs

Shared checks (apply wherever the check is exposed)

Check Old key New key distinct_count min, max min_distinct_count, max_distinct_count freshness column timestamp_column json_schema max_parse_failure_pct max_parse_failure_percent business_rules check predicate compare_metric tolerance tolerance_abs

docs.title: Current table is now implicit (rule 11)
docs.text:
Checks that re-declared the table under validation no longer require it; the table always comes from table_ctx, and override keys are optional defaults:

  • referential_integrity: source_schema/source_table/source_catalog are now optional, defaulting to the validated table (previously the required schema/table were reloaded by name).
  • cross_table_equality, temporal_consistency: left_schema/left_table/left_catalog are now optional, defaulting to the validated table; only the right side is required.
  • cross_gold: left_table is now optional, defaulting to the validated table; the signature is widened to (df, cfg, table_ctx).

docs.title: Dashboard generation: per-layer catalogs and optional tiers
docs.text:
generate_dashboard() / hydrate_template() (neco_dq/dashboards/lakeview.py) now support medallion tiers that live in different catalogs and dashboards that cover only some tiers.

  • layers accepts, per tier, either the existing list[str] of schemas (which live in the global catalog) or a dict {"catalog": ..., "schemas": [...]} for a tier in its own catalog. Mixed forms are allowed.
  • Tiers are optional: at least one is required; a bronze-only dashboard is valid. Absent tiers render empty widgets rather than being removed.
  • catalog is now optional (required only if a tier uses the list form). The previous single-catalog call shape is unchanged and fully backward compatible.
  • Every dataset is now scoped by a CONCAT(catalog, '.', schema) IN (...) pair predicate instead of a single catalog = '...' equality, so tiers that share a schema name across catalogs stay correctly separated. expected_tables entries resolve their catalog from layers and are matched on catalog.schema.table.
  • expected_tables accepts, per entry, either the existing (schema, table) pair (catalog resolved from layers) or an explicit (catalog, schema, table) triple; the two forms may be mixed. The triple lets a schema name that lives in more than one catalog be referenced unambiguously — a bare pair for such a schema is now rejected as ambiguous and the triple names the catalog. A triple's (catalog, schema) must be declared in layers.

docs.title: Deprecated
docs.text: • All old parameter keys listed above. They are accepted with a deprecation record this release and will be removed in the next major release, after which unknown legacy keys become errors (see docs/configuration/naming-conventions.md).

docs.title: binary_decodable crash on malformed base64 under ANSI/Photon
docs.text: The base64_json format used unbase64(), which under ANSI / Photon strict mode raises CONVERSION_INVALID_INPUT on the first non-base64 row (e.g. a column that already holds decoded JSON text), aborting the entire check instead of counting the row as a failure. It now uses try_to_binary(col, 'BASE64') (NULL on malformed input) and validates JSON structure via the first decoded byte, so bad rows are counted and evaluated against the configured threshold.
Dashboard provisioning: generate a ready-to-use Databricks AI/BI (Lakeview) dashboard on top of the DQ history table.

docs.title: DQ Dashboard Generation (Lakeview)
docs.text:
A new neco_dq.dashboards module builds a Databricks AI/BI (Lakeview) dashboard from a bundled, versioned template hydrated with your deployment's coordinates. No SQL or widgets are authored by hand: the proven queries are reused verbatim and only deployment-specific values are filled in.

Two public functions:

  • generate_dashboard(...): creates or updates a dashboard in the workspace, optionally validating every dataset query on a SQL warehouse and publishing the result. Returns a curated summary dict (dashboard_id, display_name, url, action, published).
  • hydrate_template(...): the pure function behind it. Returns the create/patch payload (fully-substituted serialized_dashboard) without any workspace I/O, useful for inspection and testing.

The dashboard is a single page with 8 datasets feeding Status, Coverage (per bronze/silver/gold tier), DQ Dimensions, Trends, KPIs, Regression, and global Filters. The bundled .lvdash.json template ships with the wheel.

Key inputs:

Parameter Purpose history_table 3-part history table used in every dataset FROM catalog Value for the WHERE catalog = '...' filter layers Medallion tier → schema(s) map; drives the layer CASE maps, schema IN (...) filters and coverage pies expected_tables (schema, table) pairs that scope the entire dashboard, not just coverage: a table you omit is invisible in every widget warehouse_id SQL warehouse (optional; auto-discovers the first RUNNING one if omitted) mode "create" (default) or "update" (requires dashboard_id)

Design notes:

  • create is intentionally not idempotent and there is no lookup-by-name: the Lakeview list API is eventually consistent, so a just-created dashboard may not appear yet. Save the dashboard_id from creation and call again with mode="update" to patch.
  • Query validation binds sel_date='All' (the "unfiltered" sentinel) so the seven datasets that reference the :sel_date Run Date parameter don't fail standalone with UNBOUND_SQL_PARAMETER.
  • This is standalone by design, not wired into run_dq(): dashboard provisioning is infrequent and needs workspace credentials a normal DQ run does not.
  • Inside a Databricks notebook nothing extra is needed. databricks-sdk ships with the runtime and WorkspaceClient() authenticates from the notebook context. Only external runs (local/CI) need pip install databricks-sdk and DATABRICKS_* env vars.
Profiling suite improvements: enhanced suggestions, modular-config output, and a refactor of the suite.

docs.title: Modular-Config Output for suggest Mode
docs.text:
suggest mode can write its suggestions directly as a modular-config directory tree that run_dq reads, instead of only flat per-suite YAML files or a Delta table. Set suggest_output.modular_config_path and it generates per-suite suite.yaml, one test_groups/<table>.yaml per table, GE configs under the owning suite's great_expectations/, and a default global/policy.yaml.

Options under suggest_output:

Option Default Effect modular_config_path (none) Directory to write the modular tree into include_policy true Write global/policy.yaml (required by the resolver) include_profiles false Write a global/profiles.yml template parameterize_catalog false Replace the catalog with {{ profile.target_catalog }} overwrite false Replace existing files (skips them on local fs otherwise) dry_run false Return the would-write paths without writing

With parameterize_catalog and include_profiles, one generated config can target dev/stg/prod by switching profile. Files are named after the table only (catalog and schema are implied by the directory layout). Implemented as a new ModularConfigOutputMixin; suggestion-generation logic is unchanged.

docs.title: New Check Suggestions
docs.text:
The suggest builders now propose additional checks:

  • distinct_count (Silver): moderate-cardinality columns
  • trend and completeness (Gold)
  • cross_table_equality (Silver): tables sharing *_id columns
  • Great Expectations: length (narrow-range string columns, backed by a new ExpectColumnValueLengthsToBeBetween handler), date_format (string columns holding dates in a consistent strftime format), and a min_rows/max_rows volume band

date_format detection samples non-null string values and proposes the first strftime format (e.g. %Y-%m-%d) that at least 90% of the sample matches. Only string columns are checked; real date/timestamp columns are typed and validated through dtype.

Cross-table layer detection gained _infer_layer_from_schema, which reads bronze/silver/gold from the schema name. Checks that need manual setup (trend, completeness, cross_table_equality, GE length, GE date_format, and volume) default to enabled: false.

docs.title: New Great Expectations Rules
docs.text:
The GE suite builder gained four column/dataset rules, each backed by a real GE expectation so they validate when enabled (previously the suite only had not_null, unique, dtype, between, values_set, regex, length):

  • date_format (ExpectColumnValuesToMatchStrftimeFormat): string values match a strftime date format. Fills the gap where dates stored as strings could only be checked with a fragile regex.
  • not_in_set (ExpectColumnValuesToNotBeInSet): blocklist for forbidden/dirty values (e.g. "N/A", "unknown", "-1").
  • distinct_values_in_set (ExpectColumnDistinctValuesToBeInSet): the column's distinct value set must be a subset of the allowed set. Set-aware enum validation, complementary to values_set which works row-by-row with a mostly tolerance.
  • multicolumn_sum (ExpectMulticolumnSumToEqual, dataset-level): per-row arithmetic invariant across columns (e.g. subtotal + tax == total).

Only date_format is also proposed by the profiling suggest builders; the other three are not reliably inferable from a snapshot and stay manual-only.

docs.title: Confidence Metadata
docs.text: Each suggestion carries _confidence (high/medium/low) and _reason so a reviewer can see why it was proposed. These _-prefixed fields are stripped from the emitted YAML by the formatter, so they appear only in the Delta-table output and in-memory results.

docs.title: Summary Report
docs.text:
suggest_output.summary_report_path writes a PROFILING_SUMMARY.md with:

  • Overview (tables profiled, total rows, total checks)
  • Tables grouped by layer (bronze/silver/gold)
  • Checks by suite with enabled/disabled tallies
  • Checks requiring manual configuration (every enabled: false check)
  • Schema highlights (JSON/date/PK-candidate/enum column counts)
  • Data quality observations (high null ratio, single-value columns, name-based PII hints)
  • A copy-paste Quick Start and a review checklist

All sections are derived from data already in the suggest results; no metrics are fabricated.

docs.title: Profiling Suite Split into Mixins
docs.text:
The profiling_dq_test_suite.py monolith (3119 lines, 89 methods) is now a package of nine responsibility-scoped mixins (discovery, column_stats, json_detection, checks, suggestions_generic, suggestions_ge, suggestions_suites, cross_table, modes) plus a shared constants.py. SparkProfilingDQTestSuite composes them via inheritance, with DQTestSuite last in the MRO so super() in the hook overrides still resolves. The main file drops to 214 lines (suite identity, hook overrides, __init__, four shared helpers, and run()).

The refactor is behavior-preserving: every method signature and the public import path are unchanged, the registry still resolves the suite, and the characterization tests stay green. The design-doc's builder/dataclass/Protocol rewrite is intentionally deferred.

docs.title: Generated Config Readability
docs.text: Generated test_groups and GE YAML now place a blank line before each check inside a checks: block, so the config is easier to scan. The spacing is valid YAML and round-trips through the resolver.

docs.title: volume Disabled by Default
docs.text: The Gold volume check now defaults to enabled: false because its history.table is a placeholder (<catalog.schema.dq_history_table>) that must be set before the check can run, matching how record_count_anomaly already behaves.

docs.title: date_format Check Skipped for %z/%Z Directives
docs.text: _handle_date_format in ge_suite_builder.py now skips the expectation entirely when the format string contains %z or %Z, emitting a logging.warning instead of raising. GE validates the format at construction using a naive datetime.now(), so %z is rejected before any data is checked. Even stripping %z, strptime fails on values like 2026-05-26T01:32:37.098+00:00 because the +00:00 suffix is not consumed. The fix is to skip rather than silently produce a broken expectation. Use the regex check to validate timezone-aware timestamp formats.

docs.title: nan String Coerced to float('nan') in Config
docs.text:
_convert_string_value (config resolver) called float() on every string, so a config value of "nan" became a real float('nan'). Downstream this crashed the GE suite: a nan inside a value_set makes nan != nan, so GE decides the suite changed under it and raises. The float branch now rejects non-finite forms (nan, inf, -inf, infinity) and keeps them as strings.

Why: profiling samples NULLs as the literal string "nan" in top_values, so any generated config carrying that value broke GE at runtime. This is also why the bug hit nan and not None: float("None") already raised and stayed a string, float("nan") silently succeeded.

docs.title: Suggested Checks Aligned to Real Check Handlers
docs.text:
An audit of the suggest builders against the checks each suite actually implements found suggestions that mapped to no handler, plus suggestions enabled as blocking on evidence too weak to support it. The profiling samples are statistical (approx_count_distinct, a small JSON sample), so a snapshot cannot prove uniqueness or a closed value set.

  • GE match_like and a separate _dataset.row_count key were emitted but had no handler in ge_suite_builder.py, so enabling them did nothing (silent no-op). match_like is removed (redundant with the existing regex rule); the volume suggestion now emits min_rows/max_rows, the keys the builder actually handles.
  • unique (GE), uniqueness (Gold), and idempotency (Silver) were suggested enabled: true and blocking from an approximate distinct ratio. They are now blocking only when the column(s) come from a Unity Catalog primary key; otherwise suggested enabled: false with a review comment, so a guess never blocks a pipeline.
  • mandatory_fields (Bronze) dropped from error/blocking to a non-blocking warning. 0% nulls in a snapshot is an observation, not a contract; an optional field can be null later.
  • json_schema (Silver/Gold) defaults to enabled: false when required_fields/field_types were inferred from a sample, because an optional field absent from the sample would make the check fail on first run.
  • distinct_count (Silver) is no longer suggested for date/timestamp or id-like columns: their distinct count grows over time, so a fixed max guarantees false positives.
  • completeness (Gold) is no longer suggested for free-text columns. It is now gated on _is_enum_column, matching the gate the GE values_set suggestion already used.

docs.title: GE Check Names in the History Table
docs.text:
GE_CHECK_NAME_MAP in the result normalizer was missing entries for length and the four new GE rules, so those checks were written to the history table under their raw GE type (e.g. expect_column_value_lengths_to_be_between) instead of the framework name. They now map to length, date_format, not_in_set, distinct_values_in_set, and multicolumn_sum, matching the names used elsewhere. Investigation-query templates were added for length, not_in_set, and distinct_values_in_set.

Why: the writer is schema-driven and never dropped the rows, so the bug was silent. Reports and the results viewer just showed an inconsistent raw name for these checks.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Aligned neco_dq/docs/test-suites/great-expectations.md and profiling.md with the current behavior:

  • GE doc: documented every column and dataset rule the builder actually handles, including the ones that were missing (nullable, length, date_format, not_in_set, distinct_values_in_set, integrity.pair_gt, integrity.pair_eq, multicolumn_sum). Added enabled: true to the rule examples that were missing it; without it a GE rule is skipped silently, so the old examples were copy-paste traps. Added a timezone limitation note to date_format: formats with %z/%Z are not supported (see Fixed section); the regex check is the documented alternative.
  • Profiling doc: corrected mandatory_fields to non-blocking warning, documented the primary-key-vs-candidate rule for uniqueness checks (enabled+blocking only with a UC primary key), added the distinct_count date/id carve-out, the gold completeness/trend suggestions, the GE date_format suggestion, and the min_rows/max_rows volume band. Added documentation for the previously undocumented output options: modular_config_path (with all sub-options: include_profiles, include_policy, parameterize_catalog, overwrite, dry_run) and summary_report_path. Delta table section updated to note that the table is created automatically and each run overwrites it.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• block_on_threshold now evaluates the global failure rate across all suites, not per-suite

    Why: The terminal logger shows a global success rate (total passed / total checks across all engines), but the policy was comparing the threshold against each engine individually. A suite with few checks but many failures (e.g., 4 fails on 5 checks = 80%) could trigger blocking even when the global rate was well below the configured threshold (e.g., 1.6% across 255 total checks). The fix aggregates total_checks and failed across all engines before comparing against failure_threshold, making the policy consistent with what the summary displays. Two regression tests added.
Multi-environment configuration support via profiles.

docs.title: Profiles System
docs.text:
New profiles.yaml file enables environment-specific configuration (dev/stg/prod):

# profiles.yml
profiles:
  dev:
    target_catalog: analytics_dev
    variables:
      freshness_hours: 48
      min_record_count: 100

  prod:
    target_catalog: analytics_prod
    variables:
      freshness_hours: 12
      min_record_count: 10000

default_profile: dev

docs.title: Jinja2 Variables in Config
docs.text:
Use {{ profile.* }} and {{ var.* }} in any YAML config:

Variable Description {{ profile.name }} Active profile name (e.g., "dev", "prod") {{ profile.target_catalog }} Catalog from profile {{ var.* }} Any custom variable defined in variables: 
tables:
  - catalog: "{{ profile.target_catalog }}"
    schema: bronze
    table: orders
    checks:
      freshness:
        enabled: true
        max_delay_hours: "{{ var.freshness_hours }}"
      mandatory_fields:
        enabled: true
        columns: "{{ var.mandatory_columns }}"

All types are auto-converted: strings, numbers, booleans, and lists.

docs.title: New profile Parameter
docs.text:
from neco_dq.runner import run_dq

# Explicit profile
run_dq("/path/to/config", profile="prod")

# From environment variable (NECO_DQ_PROFILE=prod)
run_dq("/path/to/config")

docs.title: Profile Policy Overrides
docs.text:
Override DQ policy per environment:

profiles:
  dev:
    target_catalog: analytics_dev
    policy:
      failure_threshold: 0.5   # block only if >50% fail
      block_on_threshold: false
      block_test_suites:
        bronze: false          # don't block on bronze in dev

  prod:
    target_catalog: analytics_prod
    policy:
      failure_threshold: 0.05  # block if >5% fail
      block_on_threshold: true # FAIL if threshold exceeded (even non-blocking)

Profile policy values override global/policy.yaml. block_test_suites is deep-merged.

docs.title: Profile Inheritance
docs.text:
Profiles can extend other profiles using extends:

profiles:
  base:
    variables:
      freshness_hours: 24
      min_record_count: 1000

  dev:
    extends: base
    target_catalog: analytics_dev
    variables:
      freshness_hours: 48  # override base

  prod:
    extends: base
    target_catalog: analytics_prod
  • Child values override parent values
  • Variables are deep-merged (child adds/overrides, parent values preserved)
  • Multi-level inheritance supported (child → parent → grandparent)
  • Circular inheritance detected and raises CircularInheritanceError

docs.title: Profile Resolution Order
docs.text:
1. Explicit profile parameter (highest priority)
  2. NECO_DQ_PROFILE environment variable
  3. default_profile from profiles.yml
  4. "default" fallback

docs.title: Profile Context in Execution Trace
docs.text:
When profiles are used, check results include profile info in the execution field:

execution:
  duration_ms: 1234
  rows_scanned: 50000
  profile:
    name: "prod"
    target_catalog: "analytics_prod"

This enables: - Traceability: Know which profile was used for each check result - Debugging: "This failed in prod but not in dev", check execution.profile - Audit: Historical results show the environment context

The profile field is only present when profiles are actively used (not when using single-file configs without profiles).

docs.title: Enhanced Slack Alerts
docs.text:
Redesigned Slack notifications with consolidated summary format:

*Data Quality Summary*
`qa` • 2026-06-12 15:30 UTC

*Status:* *FAIL* (3 blocking)
*Success Rate:* 90.2% (55/61 checks)  •  Threshold: 10%

bronze         🟨    10/11
silver         🟩    15/15
gold           🟥    30/35

*Top Failures:*
• `freshness` → gold.aggregated_metrics (summary_created_at)
• `referential_integrity` → gold.aggregated_metrics (record_id)

New Slack options:

Option Default Description send_always false Send on PASS and WARN (not just FAIL) mention_on_fail false Add @channel mention on FAIL include_job_link true Include Databricks job URL max_failures_shown 5 Max failures in Top Failures list compact_mode false Single-line summary format 
alerts:
  slack:
    enabled: true
    send_always: true
    mention_on_fail: true

Other improvements: - Profile name shown in Slack message (if not "default") - Environment auto-detected from Databricks workspace URL (hidden if "unknown") - Colored squares for suite status: 🟥 FAIL, 🟨 WARN, 🟩 PASS - Job link only shown when running on Databricks

docs.text: Module Purpose neco_dq/config/context.py DQContext dataclass for runtime profile data neco_dq/config/profile_loader.py Load and resolve profiles from profiles.yml

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• resolve_config() now accepts optional context: DQContext parameter
  • run_dq() now accepts optional profile: str parameter
  • All internal config functions propagate context for Jinja2 rendering
  • _build_execution_trace() now includes profile when profile context is set
  • failure_threshold is now informational only: shown in summary and policy message when exceeded
  • Blocking failures always cause FAIL regardless of threshold
  • Non-blocking failures always cause WARN (threshold doesn't suppress warnings)
  • Summary now shows threshold when configured: Success Rate: 85.7% │ Threshold: 10% │ Status: WARN
  • Policy message includes threshold detail when exceeded: DQ completed with WARNINGS (failure rate exceeds 10% threshold)
  • New block_on_threshold policy option: when true, non-blocking failures exceeding threshold cause FAIL instead of WARN

docs.title: Check Logic Improvements
docs.text:
Silver Suite: - _check_status_transition: Replaced .collect() with Spark window functions to prevent OOM on large datasets - _check_totals_consistency: Now correctly detects headers with non-zero amounts but no detail rows (previously silent pass)

Gold Suite: - _check_reconciliation_expr: Fixed join filter bug when gold and silver use different column names - _check_coverage: Replaced fillna() with coalesce() for proper NULL handling in outer joins - _check_completeness: Replaced .collect() with Spark-native operations for serverless compatibility - _extract_metric_from_details: Improved robustness with multiple extraction patterns for historical trend analysis

Shared Checks: - _check_json_schema: Empty data now returns warning message instead of silent pass - _check_freshness: Properly handles timezones (converts all timestamps to UTC for comparison)

Bronze Suite: - _check_binary_version_header_check: NULL values now correctly fail instead of silently passing

docs.title: Error Messages
docs.text: • Misleading error on invalid config path: When a non-existent path was passed to run_dq(), the error incorrectly suggested it was a missing template tag. Now shows a clear message: Config path not found: 'path/'. Ensure the path exists and points to a valid YAML file or modular config directory.

docs.title: Backward Compatibility
docs.text: Profiles are 100% optional. Existing configurations work without any changes: - No profiles.yaml file required - Hardcoded values in configs still work - Use {{ var.x | default(y) }} for gradual migration
Enhanced debugging capabilities with statistics-only failure analysis. No PII exposure.

docs.title: Four-Layer Result Structure
docs.text:
Every check result now includes 4 layers of information:

Layer Purpose When Present details Human-readable message (~60 chars) Always failure_stats Aggregate statistics (counts, distributions) Only on FAIL investigation_query SQL template for debugging Only on FAIL execution Performance context (duration, row counts) Always

docs.title: New Helper Methods (base_test_suite.py)
docs.text:
PASS helpers: _details_pass_count(), _details_pass_bounds(), _details_pass_all(), _details_pass_comparison(), _details_pass_freshness(), _details_pass_reconciliation()

FAIL helpers: _details_fail_found(), _details_fail_missing(), _details_fail_exceeds(), _details_fail_below(), _details_fail_above(), _details_fail_mismatch(), _details_fail_deviation()

CONFIG/ERROR helpers: _details_config_missing(), _details_not_found(), _details_error(), _details_no_data(), _details_insufficient()

Debug builders: _build_failure_stats(), _build_investigation_query(), _build_execution_trace()

docs.title: All Suites Updated
docs.text: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Shared, and GE suites now include: - Narrative details messages - failure_stats with distributions and diagnostics - investigation_query SQL templates (16 check-specific templates) - execution trace with timing and row counts

docs.title: Standardized Detail Messages
docs.text:
All messages now start with a word (never a number):

Type Pattern Example PASS {Metric} OK: {value} "Record count OK: 5000 rows" PASS All {n} {items} {condition} "All 5000 keys unique" FAIL Found {n} {items} ({pct}%) "Found 50 duplicate keys (5.0%)" FAIL {Metric} {value} exceeds {limit} "Data age 48h exceeds 24h limit" CONFIG Missing config: {keys} "Missing config: key_column"

docs.title: Simplified System Checks
docs.text:
• data_filter: Now shows only status=ok (filter details moved to execution)
  • table_read: Now shows only status=ok (table info in execution)

docs.title: Removed (Breaking Changes)
docs.text: Removed Migration _safe_sample() method Use failure_stats for statistics include_sample config No replacement needed partial_unexpected_list (GE) Use failure_stats instead

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• NEVER stores: row values, primary keys, sample data
  • Only stores: counts, percentages, column names, query templates
  • Security review: PASSED (2026-05-28)

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• History parsing backward compatibility: Checks that read from history tables now support both old and new detail message formats
  • record_count_anomaly (Bronze): Parses count from "record_count=X" (old) and "Record count OK: X rows" (new)
  • _extract_metric_from_details (Gold): Parses metric from "metric=X", "value=X" (old), "Volume OK: X", "current=X" (new)
  • Summary unique tables count: TOTALS row now shows correct unique table count (passed from loading phase instead of recalculating)
  • Removed unused tables_list from summary engine (was computed but never consumed)
The version bump to 1.0.0 is intentional. After extensive testing and usage, we've validated that the framework is stable and ready for a 1.0 release.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Enhanced Terminal Summary: Completely redesigned DQ summary output for better clarity
  • Cleaner column headers: Checks instead of Total, removed Col Issues

  • Summary correctly deduplicates tables shared between native and GE suites

  • GE Check Name Mapping: Short, consistent names for Great Expectations checks

  • expect_column_values_to_not_be_null → not_null
  • expect_column_values_to_be_unique → unique
  • expect_column_values_to_be_between → between
  • expect_column_values_to_be_in_set → values_set
  • expect_column_values_to_match_regex → regex
  • expect_table_row_count_to_be_between → row_count
  • And 5 more mappings for common GE expectations

  • Original GE type preserved in extra_metadata["ge_expectation_type"]

  • GE Progress Bar Control: Configure progress bar visibility via verbose parameter

  • verbose=True: GE progress bars visible
  • Uses ProgressBarsConfig in GE DataContextConfig

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Tag-Based Check Selector: Run only checks with specific tags across all suites
  • New tags parameter in run_dq(): run_dq(config, tags=["critical", "daily"])
  • Configure tags at check level: tags: [critical, daily, smoke]
  • Strict filtering: checks without tags are skipped when filter is active
  • OR logic: check runs if ANY of its tags match ANY filter tag
  • Full support for Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Great Expectations suites
  • Smart pre-filtering: only tables with tagged checks are loaded
  • Suites without any tagged tables are skipped entirely
  • GE suite: tags supported at rule level (e.g., column.not_null.tags: [smoke])

docs.title: Filtering Behavior
docs.text: Scenario Behavior No tags parameter All checks run (normal behavior) tags set + check has matching tag ✅ Check runs tags set + check has non-matching tag ❌ Check skipped tags set + check has no tags ❌ Check skipped tags set + table has no tagged checks ❌ Table not loaded tags set + suite has no tagged tables ❌ Suite skipped

docs.title: Configuration Example (Bronze/Silver/Gold)
docs.text:
silver:
  tables:
    - catalog: my_catalog
      schema: my_schema
      table: orders
      checks:
        idempotency:
          enabled: true
          tags: [critical, daily]

        freshness:
          enabled: true
          tags: [daily, smoke]

        record_count:
          enabled: true
          tags: [hourly]

docs.title: Configuration Example (Great Expectations)
docs.text:
great_expectations:
  tables:
    - catalog: my_catalog
      schema: my_schema
      table: orders
      checks:
        order_id:
          not_null:
            enabled: true
            tags: [critical, smoke]   # Tag at rule level
          unique:
            enabled: true
            # No tags = skipped when filtering
        amount:
          between:
            enabled: true
            min: 0
            max: 10000
            tags: [daily]

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
from neco_dq.runner import run_dq

# Run only critical checks
results = run_dq("/Workspace/config/", tags=["critical"])

# Run daily checks across specific suites
results = run_dq(
    "/Workspace/config/",
    run_suites=["silver", "gold"],
    tags=["daily"]
)

# Run smoke tests
results = run_dq("/Workspace/config/", tags=["smoke"])

docs.title: Suggested Tag Conventions
docs.text: Tag Description critical Must pass for pipeline to proceed smoke Quick sanity checks daily Run once per day hourly Run every hour expensive Long-running checks regression Post-deployment validation

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Data Filtering for Great Expectations Suite: Full filtering support for GE suite, consistent with Bronze/Silver/Gold
  • row_filter: Suite/table-level filtering using Spark SQL syntax (supports current_date(), INTERVAL)
  • partition_filter: Partition-based filtering with dict syntax
  • row_condition: Check-level filtering using Pandas query syntax
  • defaults section support for inherited filters across all tables

  • Automatic data_filter check in results showing rows before/after filtering

  • Check-level row_condition: Filter rows for individual GE checks

  • Supported checks: not_null, nullable, unique (single column), between, values_set, regex
  • Uses Pandas query syntax (e.g., "status == 'ACTIVE'")
  • Useful for conditional validation (e.g., validate shipping_date only when status == 'SHIPPED')

docs.title: Configuration Example
docs.text:
great_expectations:
  defaults:
    row_filter: "batch_ingestion_at >= current_date() - INTERVAL 7 DAYS"  # Spark SQL

  tables:
    - catalog: my_catalog
      schema: my_schema
      table: orders
      checks:
        order_id:
          not_null:
            enabled: true
            severity: critical

        shipping_date:
          not_null:
            enabled: true
            row_condition: "status == 'SHIPPED'"  # Pandas query
            severity: warning

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
• row_filter uses Spark SQL → dynamic dates work (current_date() - INTERVAL 7 DAYS)
  • row_condition uses Pandas query → static values only, no SQL functions
  • For date filtering, prefer row_filter over row_condition

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Kendall W Label Validation: Enhanced kendall_w observed metric with consensus label validation
  • New label parameter: Static expected label (e.g., "strong", "moderate", "low")
  • New label_column parameter: Column name containing expected label per row/group
  • New thresholds parameter: Custom thresholds dict for label classification
  • Validates observed consensus level against expected label

  • Returns detailed mismatch errors when label validation fails

  • Configurable Thresholds: DEFAULT_KENDALL_W_THRESHOLDS now includes "low": 0.2 label

  • Default thresholds: strong (≥0.9), moderate (≥0.7), fair (≥0.5), weak (≥0.3), low (≥0.2), none (<0.2)

  • Custom thresholds can be provided via thresholds config parameter

  • Configurable Minimum Raters: New min_raters parameter for Kendall W calculation

  • min_raters: 2 (default): Requires at least 2 raters, statistically correct
  • min_raters: 1: Allows single-rater calculations for compatibility with source systems

docs.title: Improved
docs.text:
• Better Error Reporting: Label mismatch errors now include totals for better visibility
  • Format: kendall_w_label_mismatch: 93/150 failed (57 passed); group=(...): observed=weak, expected=moderate
  • Shows failed count, total groups, and passed count at a glance

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Refactored _kendall_w function into smaller helper functions for better maintainability:
  • _build_expected_labels_map(): Builds group → label mapping from DataFrame column
  • _format_label_mismatch_error(): Formats error messages for label mismatches
  • _prepare_kendall_w_dataframe(): Prepares DataFrame for Kendall W calculation
  • _kendall_w_grouped(): Handles grouped calculation with label validation
  • _kendall_w_ungrouped(): Handles ungrouped calculation with label validation

docs.title: Example Configuration
docs.text:
compare_metric:
  metric:
    type: kendall_w
    column: items
    rank_sum_field: mean_rank
    appearances_field: item_appearances_n
    group_by: [record_id, question_id]
    label_column: consensus_level    # Expected label from column
    min_raters: 1                    # Allow single-rater calculations
    thresholds:                      # Custom thresholds
      strong: 0.9
      moderate: 0.3
      low: 0.2
  expected_from:
    type: column_value
    column: kendall_w
    group_by: [record_id, question_id]
  operator: "~"
  tolerance: 0.01

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Verbose Mode: New verbose parameter in run_dq() to control output verbosity
  • verbose=False (default): Clean logs, progress bars hidden
  • verbose=True: Debug logging level, progress bars visible
  • Hides Great Expectations tqdm progress bars by default (TQDM_DISABLE=1)

docs.title: Improved

• Logging System: Streamlined and unified terminal logs for better readability
  • Unified logger name: neco_dq across all components (previously DQ Runner, Orchestrator, ConfigResolver, DQResultWriter, GEDQTestSuite, DQAlerts)

  • Removed internal details (e.g., DQOrchestrator initialized)
  • ConfigResolver logs moved to DEBUG level (hidden by default)
  • force=True in logging.basicConfig for Databricks compatibility

docs.text:

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Failure Threshold: Optional failure_threshold parameter in dq_policy
  • Blocks pipeline only when failure rate exceeds the configured threshold
  • Example: failure_threshold: 0.1 blocks only if >10% of checks fail
  • Backward compatible: no threshold = current behavior (any blocking failure blocks)
  • Per-suite evaluation: each suite's failure rate is calculated independently

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Removed unused fail_on_error parameter from DQFailurePolicy
  • Severity-based warnings: Non-blocking failures with critical or error severity now trigger DQ_WARN (exit code 10)
  • Previously only severity: warning triggered warnings
  • severity: low or info with blocking: false still returns SUCCESS

docs.title: Exit Code Hierarchy (Updated)
docs.text: Condition Exit Code blocking: true + failed DQ_ERROR (20) blocking: false + severity: critical/error/warning + failed DQ_WARN (10) blocking: false + severity: low/info + failed SUCCESS (0)

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
dq_policy:
  failure_threshold: 0.1  # Block only if >10% of checks fail
  block_test_suites:
    bronze: true
    silver: true

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Custom Test Suites: Load custom test suites from external Python files
  • New custom_suite_files parameter in run_dq() function
  • Supports single path or list of paths for multiple custom suites
  • Dynamic loading of DQTestSuite subclasses from any Python file
  • Automatic suite name derivation from class name (CamelCase → snake_case)

  • Support for local paths and /Workspace/ paths (Databricks)

  • Registry Functions: New functions in test_suite_registry.py

  • load_custom_suite_from_file(file_path) - Load suite class from Python file
  • register_custom_suite(name, class) - Register custom suite in registry

  • _derive_suite_config_key(class_name, path) - Derive config key from class name

  • Documentation: Complete guide for custom test suites

  • docs/test-suites/custom.md - Usage examples and best practices
  • Check method signature documentation
  • Helper methods reference

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
# my_custom_suite.py
class MyCustomSuite(DQTestSuite):
    @property
    def _suite_name(self) -> str:
        return "my_custom"

    @property
    def _suite_config_key(self) -> str:
        return "my_custom"

    def _check_my_validation(self, df, cfg):
        # Custom check logic
        return True, "ok", None

# Run with single custom suite
from neco_dq.runner import run_dq

run_dq(
    config_ref="/Workspace/dq-config/",
    custom_suite_files="/Workspace/my_custom_suite.py"
)

# Run with multiple custom suites
run_dq(
    config_ref="/Workspace/dq-config/",
    custom_suite_files=[
        "/Workspace/order_checks.py",
        "/Workspace/customer_checks.py",
    ]
)

docs.title: Configuration Example
docs.text:
# dq-config/my_custom.yaml
my_custom:
  tables:
    - catalog: my_catalog
      schema: my_schema
      table: my_table
      checks:
        my_validation:
          enabled: true
          severity: error

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Data Filtering System: Filter data before running DQ checks
  • row_filter: SQL WHERE expression applied to table data
  • partition_filter: Dict-based partition filtering with automatic SQL conversion
  • Suite-level defaults section for inherited filters
  • Table-level overrides for granular control
  • Filter metadata included in results (filters_applied)

  • Empty result handling with no_rows_after_filter warning

  • Partition Auto-Discovery: Automatically detect and filter on table partitions

  • partition_filter: {auto: true} - filter on latest partition value
  • partition_filter: {auto_latest: N} - filter on latest N partition values
  • Reads partition metadata via DESCRIBE DETAIL
  • Validates partition columns and warns if non-partition columns used

  • Works with single and multi-column partitions

  • Extended Filter Metadata: Rich details in data_filter check for traceability

  • rows_before / rows_after: Row counts before and after filtering
  • filter_ratio: Percentage of rows remaining after filter
  • row_filter / partition_filter: Actual SQL expressions applied
  • auto_discovery: Partition auto-resolution details

docs.title: Configuration Example
docs.text:
silver:
  defaults:
    row_filter: "status != 'DELETED'"
    # Auto-discover partitions (recommended)
    partition_filter:
      auto: true
  tables:
    - catalog: my_catalog
      schema: my_schema
      table: orders
      # Explicit partition values (overrides auto)
      partition_filter:
        date: "2024-01-15"

docs.title: Code Quality & Best Practices
docs.text: This guide covers coding standards, patterns, and best practices specific to the Neco DQ Framework.

docs.title: Architecture Principles
docs.text:
For architecture principles, component ownership, and design patterns, see:

  • Architecture Overview - System components and execution flow
  • Governance - Component boundaries, anti-patterns, and design patterns

docs.title: Standard Signature
docs.text:
All checks MUST follow this contract:

def _check_<name>(
    self,
    df: DataFrame,
    cfg: dict[str, Any]
) -> tuple[bool, str, str | None]:
    """
    Brief description.

    Config:
        param1: type - Description
        param2: type - Description (optional)

    Returns:
        (passed, details, column)
    """
    pass

docs.title: Return Contract
docs.text:
Every check returns a 3-tuple:

Element Type Description passed bool True if check passed details str Human-readable narrative (~60 chars, starts with a word) column str \| None Column name or None for table-level

Good details format (v1.1.0+): 

# PASS patterns
"All 5000 keys unique"
"Record count OK: 1523 rows"
"Volume OK: 700 (within 500-1000)"

# FAIL patterns
"Found 50 duplicate keys (5.0% of 1000)"
"Missing 3 required columns"
"Data age 48h exceeds 24h limit"

Bad details format: 

"check failed"  # Too vague
"error"         # No context
"5"             # Never start with a number

docs.title: Generalization Requirement
docs.text: Every check MUST be generic and reusable across any dataset.

docs.title: Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Names must describe behavior, not business domain:

Bad (Business-specific) Good (Generic) _check_row_count _check_row_count _check_payment_flow _check_status_transition _check_rating_aggregation _check_compare_metric

docs.title: Parameter Names
docs.text:
Use standardized generic parameter names (full rules in Naming conventions):

Parameter Type Purpose column str Single column name columns list[str] Multiple column names key_columns str \| list[str] Primary/composite key timestamp_column str Timestamp field value_column str Numeric value field group_by list[str] Grouping columns filter str SQL WHERE clause threshold dict Row-level failure threshold tolerance float Value comparison tolerance operator str Comparison operator

docs.title: Example: Generic vs Business-Specific
docs.text:
# BAD - Business-specific
def _check_value_range(self, df, cfg):
    return df.filter(col("rating").between(1, 5)).count() == df.count()

# GOOD - Generic and reusable
def _check_value_in_range(self, df: DataFrame, cfg: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[bool, str, str | None]:
    """Validates column values are within specified range."""
    column = cfg["column"]
    min_val = cfg["min_value"]
    max_val = cfg["max_value"]

    invalid_count = df.filter(~col(column).between(min_val, max_val)).count()
    passed = invalid_count == 0

    return passed, f"invalid_count={invalid_count}, range=[{min_val}, {max_val}]", column

docs.title: Preferred Patterns
docs.text:
# Use DataFrame API
df.filter(col("status") == "active").count()

# Explicit casts
df.withColumn("amount", col("amount").cast("decimal(10,2)"))

# Explicit null filtering
df.filter(col("email").isNotNull())

# Narrow transformations when possible
df.select("id", "name").filter(col("active"))

docs.title: Avoid
docs.text:
# Implicit schema inference
spark.read.json(path)  # Use .schema() instead

# Unnecessary actions
df.count()  # Only when needed
df.collect()  # Avoid on large datasets

# Full scans when aggregations suffice
df.collect()  # Use df.agg() instead

docs.title: Composite Key Handling
docs.text:
Support both single string and list:

key_cols = cfg["key_columns"]

# Normalize to list
if isinstance(key_cols, str):
    key_cols = [k.strip() for k in key_cols.split(",")]

# Use normalized list
dupes = df.groupBy(*key_cols).agg(count("*").alias("cnt"))

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
Checks should handle errors gracefully:

def _check_example(self, df: DataFrame, cfg: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[bool, str, str | None]:
    try:
        column = cfg["column"]

        if column not in df.columns:
            return False, f"column_not_found: {column}", column

        # ... perform validation ...
        return passed, details, column

    except KeyError as e:
        return False, f"missing_config_parameter: {e}", None

    except Exception as e:
        return False, f"check_error: {e!s}", cfg.get("column")

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• All public functions must have type hints
  • Use from __future__ import annotations for forward references
  • Use dict[str, Any] for configuration dictionaries

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any
from pyspark.sql import DataFrame

def resolve_metric(
    spark: SparkSession,
    df: DataFrame,
    cfg: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[bool, str, str | None]:
    """Resolve a metric comparison."""
    ...

docs.title: Docstring Format
docs.text:
def _check_value_in_range(
    self,
    df: DataFrame,
    cfg: dict[str, Any]
) -> tuple[bool, str, str | None]:
    """
    Validates column values fall within specified numeric range.

    Use case: Ensure values are within valid bounds (e.g., ratings 1-5).

    Config:
        column: str - Column name to validate
        min_value: numeric - Minimum allowed value (inclusive)
        max_value: numeric - Maximum allowed value (inclusive)

    Returns:
        (passed, details, column)

    Example config:
        ```yaml
        value_in_range:
          enabled: true
          column: rating
          min_value: 1
          max_value: 5
        ```
    """
    pass

docs.title: Required Sections
docs.text:
1. Brief description (one line)
  2. Use case (when to use)
  3. Config parameters with types
  4. Returns explanation
  5. Example config (for complex checks)

docs.title: Ruff Configuration
docs.text:
Ruff is the primary linting and formatting tool. Key rules:

Rule Code What It Checks Security S Hardcoded passwords, SQL injection Print T20 Use of print() statements Datetime DTZ Timezone-naive datetime Naming N PEP8 naming conventions Pylint PL Complexity, too many arguments Bugbear B Common bugs

docs.title: Validation Workflow
docs.text:
# Check for issues
ruff check .

# Auto-fix and format
ruff check --fix . && ruff format .

# Verify clean
ruff check . && ruff format --check .

Never present Python code that fails ruff validation.

docs.title: Common Fixes
docs.text:
Print statements: 

# Wrong
print(f"Processing {table}")

# Correct
import logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.info(f"Processing {table}")

Timezone-naive datetime: 

# Wrong
from datetime import datetime
now = datetime.now()

# Correct
from datetime import datetime, timezone
now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

docs.title: Anti-Patterns
docs.text: For the complete list of forbidden patterns and prohibited technologies, see Governance - Anti-Patterns.

docs.title: Validation Checklist
docs.text: Before submitting code, verify:

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
• [ ] Function name is generic (no business terms)
  • [ ] Parameter names are generic
  • [ ] Uses standard parameter names

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
• [ ] Works for any dataset
  • [ ] Handles composite keys (normalize to list)
  • [ ] Graceful error handling
  • [ ] No hardcoded business logic

docs.title: Return Values
docs.text:
• [ ] Returns tuple[bool, str, str | None]
  • [ ] Details are narrative (~60 chars, starts with word)
  • [ ] Column is name, comma-separated list, or None

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
• [ ] Passes ruff check .
  • [ ] Passes ruff format --check .
  • [ ] Type hints present
  • [ ] Docstring with config parameters

docs.title: Where Changes Belong
docs.text:
Change Type Location New metric neco_dq/core/metrics/ New operator neco_dq/core/metrics/operators.py New validation neco_dq/test_suites/<layer>/ New failure semantics neco_dq/core/policy/ New visualization neco_dq/core/summary/ New notification channel neco_dq/core/alerts/

If a change requires edits across multiple areas, it's likely incorrect.

docs.title: Contribution Guide
docs.text: This guide covers the contribution process for Neco DQ Framework, including branch naming, pull requests, testing requirements, and feedback collection.

docs.title: 1. Set Up Development Environment
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11 or newer. The repository is managed with uv (see the root CONTRIBUTING.md for the authoritative setup):

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/woven-by-toyota/neco-dq-framework.git
cd neco-dq-framework

# Create the environment with all dev dependencies (includes PySpark)
uv sync --extra dev --frozen

# Install pre-commit hooks
uv run pre-commit install

docs.title: 2. Create a Feature Branch
docs.text:
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git checkout -b feat/<description>

docs.title: 3. Make Changes and Validate
docs.text:
Run tools inside the managed environment with uv run:

# Lint and format
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .

# Run tests (or the make shortcut: `make test`)
uv run pytest tests/

docs.title: 4. Submit Pull Request
docs.text:
• Follow the PR template below
  • Ensure all tests pass
  • Update CHANGELOG.md for user-facing changes

docs.title: Golden Path: MVP Features
docs.text: The following features solve 90% of daily DQ tasks. Master these before exploring advanced options.

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text: Feature Layer Description Documentation Modular Config All Directory-based YAML configuration Modular Config freshness Bronze Check data recency Bronze Suite mandatory_fields Bronze Verify required columns exist Bronze Suite schema_drift Bronze Detect schema changes Bronze Suite idempotency Silver Check for duplicate keys Silver Suite referential_integrity Silver Validate foreign key relationships Silver Suite compare_metric Silver/Gold Compare computed vs expected values Compare Metric uniqueness Gold Ensure unique business keys Gold Suite GE Integration All Great Expectations column checks GE Suite Data Filtering All row_filter, partition_filter Data Filtering

docs.title: Decision Tree: Which Check to Use?
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Start[Need to validate data?] --> Bronze
    Start --> Silver
    Start --> Gold

    subgraph Bronze["Bronze (Raw/Ingestion)"]
        B1[Schema correct?] --> B1R[schema_drift]
        B2[Required fields?] --> B2R[mandatory_fields]
        B3[Data recent?] --> B3R[freshness]
        B4[Record count normal?] --> B4R[record_count_anomaly]
    end

    subgraph Silver["Silver (Transformation)"]
        S1[No duplicates?] --> S1R[idempotency]
        S2[FK valid?] --> S2R[referential_integrity]
        S3[Counts match source?] --> S3R[flow_completeness]
        S4[Numeric comparison?] --> S4R[compare_metric]
    end

    subgraph Gold["Gold (Aggregation)"]
        G1[Unique business keys?] --> G1R[uniqueness]
        G2[Coverage complete?] --> G2R[coverage]
        G3[Metrics correct?] --> G3R[compare_metric]
        G4[Cross-table reconciliation?] --> G4R[reconciliation_expr]
    end

docs.title: Running DQ Checks
docs.text:
from neco_dq.runner import run_dq

# Run all configured checks
result = run_dq("/Workspace/path/to/config/")

# Run specific suites only
result = run_dq(
    "/Workspace/path/to/config/",
    run_suites=["bronze", "silver"]
)

docs.title: Branch Naming Rules
docs.text:
Type Pattern Example Feature feat/<description> feat/add-json-schema-check Bug Fix fix/<description> fix/compare-metric-null-handling Hotfix hotfix/<description> hotfix/critical-policy-bug Refactor refactor/<description> refactor/extract-shared-checks Docs docs/<description> docs/update-metrics-reference Test test/<description> test/add-bronze-coverage Chore chore/<description> chore/update-dependencies

Rules:

  • Always use lowercase with hyphens
  • Keep descriptions concise (3-5 words)

docs.title: Commit Message Format
docs.text:
All commits must follow Conventional Commits:

<type>: <description>

[optional body]

The scope is optional. Valid types: feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore, build, ci, revert.

Examples:

docs.title: Governance and Architecture
docs.text: This document defines component ownership, boundaries, and architectural decisions for the Neco DQ Framework.

docs.title: Scope Definition
docs.text:
neco_dq is a Data Quality validation platform for Spark/Databricks environments.

Responsibility In Scope Out of Scope Data Validation Schema, completeness, consistency, freshness Data transformation, ETL Configuration YAML parsing, template expansion, modular configs Pipeline orchestration Execution Test suite orchestration, result collection Job scheduling Reporting Summary generation, Slack alerts Dashboards, BI tools Integration Great Expectations, Databricks Other DQ tools (dbt tests, Soda)

│   ├── orchestrators/         │ Test suite coordination

docs.text: Category Required Version Rationale Data Processing PySpark >= 3.5.0 Databricks standard Configuration PyYAML >= 6.0 Industry standard Templating Jinja2 >= 3.1 Mature, secure DQ Integration Great Expectations >= 1.9.0 Enterprise DQ Expression Eval asteval >= 0.9.30 Safe Python expressions Data Analysis pandas >= 2.0, < 3.0 PySpark compatibility
